tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[segments on the round sphere]

Source: petersen:page-0195, petersen:page-0196 ↗ lem:pet-ch5-distance-function-segments 1. ch5:5.3.5On $S^n(1)\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}$ with the warped product structure $ds_n^2=dr^2+\sin ^2(r)ds_{n-1}^2$ centered at $p$: antipodal $p,q$ correspond to $r=0,\pi $; otherwise $p=(a,x_0)$, $q=(b,x_0)\in (0,\pi )\times S^{n-1}$, and $r$ is smooth on $U\simeq (0,\pi )\times S^{n-1}$. In either case any minimizing curve has length $\ge \pi $ resp. $\ge |r(p)-r(q)|$, realized by great-circle arcs. \end{example}
Proof

↗ ex:pet-ch5-sphere-segments \sketch For antipodal endpoints, apply section 3 on $[\epsilon ,b-\epsilon ]$ and let $\epsilon \to 0$ to obtain $L(c)\ge \pi $; great-circle arcs attain equality. For nonantipodal endpoints, the integral curve of $\nabla r$ minimizes inside $U$. A curve leaving $U$ passes through a pole and has length at least $\min \{ r(p)+r(q),2\pi -r(p)-r(q)\} \ge |r(p)-r(q)|$.

□
